title: Purification of Replisomes from Xenopus laevis Egg Extract for Cryo-EM Analysis
author: Passaretti, Cvetkovic, et al.
materials: Xenopus laevis low-speed supernatant egg extract

15.SDS-PAGE and silver staining.a.Load 20 μL of the samples generated in step 14 (Ch, ChPel, Inp, DP and IP) on a NuPAGE 4%–12% Bis-Tris gradient 15 well gel and run at 200 V for 45 min (Bio-Rad PowerPac).b.Stain the gel using SilverQuest kit, or any other suitable silver staining kit.
Note: The gel is fixed, sensitized, stained, and developed with provided solutions. More details are available from the manufacturer (link). An equivalent silver staining procedure can be used.
CRITICAL: To reduce the chance of sample loss due to protein complexes falling apart over time, we suggest skipping point 15 and proceeding directly with negative staining (Point 16).
16.Sample preparation for negative stain electron microscopy (NS-EM).a.Glow discharge grids coated with continuous carbon (EM Resolutions C300Cu) with a glow discharger or plasma cleaner. We used a GloQube Plus unit (Quorum Technology), with the following parameters: 25 mA current, 60 s duration and negative polarity.Note: Make sure that grids are placed in the glow discharge unit with their carbon film surface facing up. Glow discharging will make this surface hydrophilic, enabling uniform spreading of the aqueous sample and particle absorption on carbon.b.Cool down 2% uranyl acetate (UA) solution aliquot by placing it on ice for 5–10 min.c.Spin UA at 20,000 × g for 4 min at 4°C on a benchtop centrifuge (Eppendorf 5424R) to separate any precipitates and keep the UA solution at 20°C–25°C during sample preparation.Note: Protect UA from light to avoid precipitation. Keep UA solution aliquots in Eppendorf tubes wrapped in aluminum foil. While performing steps that involve UA manipulation, follow safety guidelines for working with radioactive material, including safe disposal of any contaminated item.d.Pipet three 30 μL droplets of UA solution onto a piece of parafilm from the top of the Eppendorf tube. Take care not to perturb any precipitate that might be present at the bottom of the tube (Figure 8A).Figure 8Negative staining of the grids(A) Set-up for negative staining with grids in tweezers and UA droplets on parafilm.(B) Staining of a grid on the first UA droplet.(C) Blotting away residual UA solution.e.Hold a grid by the rim using crossover locking tweezers. Place the tweezers on the bench with the glow discharged carbon surface of the grid facing upwards (Figure 8A).f.Apply 4 μL of the sample (from point 14.L) on the top surface of the grid and wait 1.5 min.Note: Incubation time can vary from one to two min. Increased incubation time can lead to some increase of particle absorption on carbon.g.Blot away the sample by touching the edge of the grid using Whatman filter paper (as shown in Figure 8C).h.Using the locked tweezers invert the grid and put it in contact with the first UA droplet, gently swirling it for 20 s, without ever breaking surface tension. Make sure that only one side of the grid is exposed to the stain solution in the process (Figure 8B).i.Quickly switch to the second UA droplet, swirling the grid for another 20 s and then repeat the same operation on the third droplet. No blotting should occur while transitioning from droplet to droplet.j.After exposure to the third UA droplet, gently blot away all residual UA solution from the grid by touching the rim of the grid with Whatman filter paper (Figure 8C) and leave the grid locked with tweezers to dry on the bench.k.Once the grid is dry (2–3 min wait), place it into a grid box for room temperature storage.l.Safely dispose all contaminated material.m.If particle quality evaluated by NS-EM is satisfactory, proceed with plunge freezing on the same day. Troubleshooting 5.17.Graphene oxide (GO) application onto the grids for cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM).a.Add 10 μL of the graphene oxide stock suspension (2 mg/mL) to 80 μL of Milli-Q water and resuspend the mixture by pipetting up and down repeatedly.b.Spin down remaining larger GO agglomerates using a benchtop centrifuge (Eppendorf 5424R) at 650 × g for 1.5 min, at 20°C–25°C.c.Carefully transfer the clear top layer of the GO suspension into a new Eppendorf tube without touching the bottom of the tube. This clear GO suspension will be used for application on the grid.d.Glow discharge grids (UltrAuFoil R1.2/1.3, Au 300 mesh) using a glow discharger or plasma cleaner. We use a GloQube Plus unit with the following parameters: 45 mA current, 5 min duration and negative polarity.Note: Make sure that the grids are placed top side up during glow discharging. The manufacturers pack grids with their top sides, where the sample should be applied, facing the center of the grid box.e.Hold a grid by the rim with crossover locking tweezers and place the tweezers on the bench with the glow discharged top grid surface facing upwards.f.Pipet 3 separate droplets of 20 μL Milli-Q water per grid on a clean piece of parafilm.g.Pipet 4 μL of the clear GO suspension on the top side of the grid and wait for 2–3 min.h.Turn the grid held with the tweezers upside down and blot away GO by touching a clean Whatman filter paper with the edge of the grid.i.Immediately pick up one water droplet from the parafilm with the GO-exposed surface of the grid. The grid should be held upside down using the locked tweezers throughout this process. Without delay, blot the water droplet by touching a dry (unused) area of the Whatman filter paper.j.Repeat the previous step, using the second water droplet.k.Turn the grid back to the original orientation, with top side facing upwards, pick up the last water droplet with the bottom side of the grid (the side that was not exposed to GO) and blot it away using the Whatman filter paper.Let the grid dry for 5 min on the tweezers. Store it on a piece of clean Whatman filter paper, protected inside a Petri dish until ready for freezing.Note: GO application should be performed within a few hours before sample application and plunge freezing.18.Sample application and plunge freezing grids using a Vitrobot.a.Attach humidifier to the Vitrobot (FEI Thermo Scientific, Vitrobot Mark IV) and inject 60 mL water with a syringe (Figure 9A). After filling the cylinder, remove any air by pulling back on the syringe plunger.Figure 9Set-up for plunge freezing(A) Humidifier attached to the Vitrobot.(B) Circular blotting paper attached to blotting pads inside the Vitrobot chamber.(C) Assembled vitrification container set.(D) A grid plunged into liquid ethane on the Vitrobot.b.Attach new circular blotting paper to both blotting pads inside the Vitrobot chamber, with concave side of the paper’s inner rim facing the pad and close the chamber (Figure 9B).c.Turn on the Vitrobot.d.Set humidity to 100% and select ‘ON’ setting.e.Set temperature to 22°C.f.Inside a fume hood, assemble the vitrification container set that consists of a liquid nitrogen base container, a brass ethane cup, a grid-box holder, a spider, and an anti-contamination ring (Figure 9C). The anti-contamination ring should be placed with ridges facing up.g.Fill up the vitrification container set with liquid nitrogen (LN2), including the ethane cup, and keep the LN2 level in the base container.h.Wait until the liquid nitrogen evaporates completely from the ethane cup.Note: The ethane cup must be cold enough for ethane to liquify (its boiling temperature at atmospheric pressure is −89°C), but not too cold to solidify (melting temperature at atmospheric pressure: −183°C). To keep the cup cold, make sure that the spider that connects the LN2 bath with the ethane cup sits stably on the edge of the cup. If ethane comes into contact with liquid nitrogen, ethane will solidify almost instantaneously.i.Fill up the ethane brass cup with ethane.Note: Take care when filling up the brass cup with ethane. Rapid heat transfer that occurs when ethane is accidentally dropped into liquid nitrogen causes rapid evaporation of ethane and pressure buildup. Always wear eye protection gear when handling cryogenic substances. Ethane is highly flammable, and liquid ethane can cause frostbite on contact with unprotected skin.j.When needed, refill the liquid nitrogen base container from behind the anti-contamination ring, so that liquid nitrogen does not come into contact with liquid ethane.k.Place grid-boxes into the grid-box holder, just below the liquid nitrogen level.l.When the surface of liquid ethane turns slightly opaque, remove the spider and transfer the vitrification container set to the Vitrobot.m.For applying the sample onto grids freshly covered with graphene oxide use the following parameters.i.Blot Force on the Vitrobot set to 0.ii.Wait Time on the Vitrobot set to 60 s.iii.Blot Time in between applications on the Vitrobot set to 0.5 s.iv.Final Blot Time on the Vitrobot set to 4.0 or 4.5 s.Note: Values for Wait Time and for the final Blot Time can vary depending on the Vitrobot instrument used.n.For each of the three sequential sample applications, dispense 4 μL of sample (from step 14.m) onto the same side of the grid that was glow-discharged and coated with GO.o.After plunge freezing into liquid ethane (Figure 9D), transfer the grid into liquid nitrogen and store in a grid box until the day of the cryo-EM imaging session.Note: In our experience, the particle density observed in negative stain EM is similar to the one observed on GO-coated cryo-EM grids. Thus, based on estimates from UA-stained grids, the number of applications required to obtain suitable particle density in cryo-EM grids can be established. When plunge freezing several grids, take care to keep the LN2 level constant in the base container.

steps.title: Prime male frogs with Folligon
steps.instruction: Inject each of ~15 male Xenopus laevis with 100 IU of Folligon (PMSG) into the dorsal lymph sac using a 1 mL syringe and a 25‑G needle 5–9 days before testes removal to increase sperm yield.

steps.title: Euthanize and dissect testes
steps.instruction: Place frogs in groups of three in 0.5 L MS‑222 solution, monitor loss of reflex, then remove frogs, lay on back, cut skin, sever arteries to stop circulation, and quickly dissect testes into a cold EB‑filled Falcon tube on ice.

steps.title: Clean, chop and filter testes
steps.instruction: Wash each testis with ~2 mL EB in a Petri dish, remove blood vessels, transfer two testes to 1 mL EB, finely chop with a razor blade until no visible particles, filter the homogenate through a 25 µm nylon mesh into a 50 mL Falcon tube kept on ice.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered material at 2 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C (Megafuge 16, TX‑400 rotor).
If supernatant remains cloudy, repeat centrifugation and combine pellets.

steps.title: Demembranate sperm nuclei
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 0.5 mL SuNaSp per testis at 20‑25 °C, add 25 µL lysolecithin per testis, incubate 5 min at 20‑25 °C, assess demembranation by mixing 1 µL sperm with 1 µL SYTOX Orange and imaging (≥95 % demembranated required).

substeps.instruction: If <95 % demembranated, repeat lysolecithin treatment.
Centrifuge again at 2 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Quench lysolecithin by resuspending pellet in 500 µL SuNaSp‑BSA per testis.
Wash twice with EB, then resuspend in 100 µL EB‑glycerol per testis.

steps.title: Quantify and aliquot sperm nuclei
steps.instruction: Dilute a small aliquot of the resuspended sperm 1:100 in EB, count nuclei with a haemocytometer, dilute stock to 1000 ng DNA/µL in EB‑glycerol, aliquot 100 µL portions and store at –80 °C (mix thoroughly before each aliquot).

steps.title: Prime female frogs with Folligon
steps.instruction: Inject 10 female Xenopus laevis with 100 IU of Folligon into the dorsal lymph sac 2–7 days before eggs are needed; do not feed frogs for up to 5 days before the next injection.

steps.title: Inject Chorulon and lay eggs
steps.instruction: One day before egg collection, inject each frog with 500 IU of Chorulon, then place frogs in laying tanks containing 2.5 L 1× MMR at 19‑23 °C; collect eggs 16‑18 h post‑injection.

substeps.instruction: Discard any eggs that are white, swollen, stringy, or have debris.
Rinse good eggs with 1 L 1× MMR and remove excess buffer.

steps.title: Dejelly and pack eggs
steps.instruction: Add cysteine solution to the rinsed eggs, swirl gently until the buffer becomes cloudy, continue adding fresh cysteine until the solution clears and eggs are compacted (max 10 min exposure).

substeps.instruction: Rinse again with 1 L 1× MMR, remove apoptotic white eggs with a plastic Pasteur pipette.
Transfer eggs to 14 mL round‑bottom tubes containing 1 mL UEB buffer supplemented with APR, LEU, PEP (10 µg/mL each, 1000×) and cytochalasin D (50 µg/mL, 200×).
Pack eggs by centrifuging at 950 × g for 1 min at 20 °C (Avanti J‑E, JS‑13.1 rotor).
Remove top buffer with a Pasteur pipette, then spin‑crush at 14 600 × g for 10 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Collect and clarify low‑speed supernatant
steps.instruction: Pierce the tube with a 20‑G needle, collect the cytoplasmic layer with a 1 mL syringe, transfer to a 50 mL Falcon tube on ice, supplement with APR, LEU, PEP (10 µg/mL each), cytochalasin D (10 µg/mL, 1000×) and 15 % v/v LFB 1/50, mix gently.

substeps.instruction: Ultracentrifuge at 48 000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C (Optima LE‑80K, SW50.1 rotor).
Remove the top lipid plug with a spatula, collect the golden cytoplasmic layer and the membrane layer just below it, avoiding the gray mitochondrial layer.
Add sterile glycerol to a final 1 % v/v, mix gently.
Drop the extract into liquid nitrogen to form frozen beads, transfer beads to cryo‑tubes and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare reagents for FLAG‑IP
steps.instruction: Gather the following on ice (4 °C): 2‑chloroacetamide (20‑25 °C), caffeine (20‑25 °C), ANIB, ANIB‑sucrose, ER, CHX, CaCl₂, sperm DNA, Cdc45‑FLAG5 (Addgene #208796, stock 47 µM), aphidicolin; switch on Megafuge 16 (TX‑400 rotor) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Activate egg extract
steps.instruction: Thaw 4 mL frozen LSS beads, add ER (40×), CHX to 0.25 mg/mL (40×), CaCl₂ to 0.3 mM (167×), and Cdc45‑FLAG5 to a final 1 µM (use the 47 µM stock), mix thoroughly, and incubate on bench at 20‑25 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Run replication reaction
steps.instruction: Add aphidicolin to 40 µM (200×) and caffeine to 5 mM (20×) final concentrations, then add demembranated sperm DNA to 20 ng/µL, mix, start timer, and incubate at 23 °C for 60 min.

steps.title: Isolate chromatin
steps.instruction: Split the 60‑min reaction into four 1 mL aliquots, add 5 mL ANIB to each, gently underlay 1 mL ANIB‑sucrose (pipette tip to bottom, do not mix), spin at 2 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, remove the ANIB phase without disturbing the sucrose cushion, wash tube walls with 1 mL ANIB (repeat 2‑3 times), then resuspend the chromatin pellet in 600 µL fresh ANIB‑sucrose.

steps.title: Sonicate and digest chromatin
steps.instruction: Sonicate the resuspended chromatin for 5 min with a Bioruptor (15 s ON / 15 s OFF, low setting), then add benzonase to 0.4 U/µL and incubate on a roller at 20‑25 °C for 30 min (sample should become transparent).

steps.title: FLAG immunoprecipitation
steps.instruction: While chromatin digests, prepare FLAG beads: transfer 100 µL magnetic FLAG beads to a microtube, wash sequentially with 1 mL PBS, PBST, PBS; block in 990 µL PBS + 10 µL 30 % BSA for 10 min at 20‑25 °C on a rotary incubator; wash with 1 mL ANIB then ANIB‑sucrose and keep in fresh ANIB‑sucrose.

substeps.instruction: Take 5 µL of the digested chromatin as a Chromatin (Ch) sample.
Spin the remaining digest at 16 900 × g for 2 min at 4 °C, collect supernatant (Input sample, 5 µL) and retain pellet (Chromatin Pellet, 5 µL).
Incubate ~600 µL supernatant with the prepared FLAG beads for 1.5 h at 4 °C on a rotary incubator.
Separate beads magnetically, collect flow‑through (5 µL, Depleted sample).
Wash beads five times: 1 mL ANIB‑sucrose, 1 mL ANIB‑sucrose + 0.1 % Triton X‑100, 1 mL ANIB‑sucrose, 1 mL IP‑EB (repeat the 2‑wash cycle).
Elute bound complexes with 200 µL IP‑EB containing 250 µM triple‑FLAG peptide; rotate 2 h at 4 °C.
Separate beads, collect 10 µL eluate as Immunoprecipitated (IP) sample (optional second elution with 50 µL IP‑EB + 1 µL FLAG peptide for 5 min, collect 10 µL as IP2).
Add 25 µL 1× LB to Ch, ChPel and DP samples, and 10 µL 2× LB to IP samples; heat at 95 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: SDS‑PAGE and silver stain
steps.instruction: Load 20 µL of each sample (Ch, ChPel, Input, Depleted, IP) onto a NuPAGE 4‑12 % Bis‑Tris gradient gel (15‑well), run at 200 V for 45 min, then stain using the SilverQuest kit (or equivalent) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Negative‑stain EM sample prep
steps.instruction: Glow‑discharge continuous‑carbon grids (25 mA, 60 s, negative polarity). Cool a 2 % uranyl acetate (UA) aliquot on ice 5‑10 min, spin at 20 000 × g for 4 min at 4 °C, keep UA at 20‑25 °C protected from light. Place three 30 µL UA droplets on parafilm, apply 4 µL of the IP sample to a grid for 1.5 min, blot with Whatman paper, then sequentially touch the grid to each UA droplet for 20 s (no blotting between droplets), blot final droplet, let grid dry 2‑3 min, store in a grid box at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare graphene‑oxide coated grids
steps.instruction: Dilute 10 µL of 2 mg/mL GO stock into 80 µL Milli‑Q water, vortex, spin at 650 × g for 1.5 min at 20‑25 °C, transfer clear supernatant. Glow‑discharge Au‑foil grids (45 mA, 5 min, negative polarity). Place grid carbon side up, add three 20 µL water droplets on parafilm, pipet 4 µL GO suspension onto grid, wait 2‑3 min, blot with Whatman paper, then sequentially pick up each water droplet and blot, repeat for all three droplets, let grid dry 5 min, store on clean Whatman paper in a petri dish until freezing.

steps.title: Plunge‑freeze grids on Vitrobot
steps.instruction: Assemble Vitrobot Mark IV with humidifier (fill with 60 mL water, remove air), attach fresh circular blotting paper, turn on Vitrobot, set humidity to 100 % and temperature to 22 °C. Prepare vitrification set: fill base container with liquid nitrogen, place brass ethane cup, let LN₂ evaporate from cup, then fill cup with liquid ethane (avoid solidification). Load graphene‑oxide coated grids, set Vitrobot parameters: Blot Force 0, Wait Time 60 s, Blot Time 0.5 s between applications, Final Blot Time 4.0‑4.5 s. Apply 4 µL sample to grid three times (same side), blot according to settings, plunge into liquid ethane, transfer grid to liquid nitrogen, store in a grid box until cryo‑EM data collection.
